page: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores of an AMD EPYC 7571 processor running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The server is configured with 16.0 GB of DDR4 system memory running at 3 GHz, delivering 4.0 GB of memory per core. It lacks integrated local storage, requiring network-attached storage volumes for file systems, and includes a 1 Gbps baseline network capability without bundled hardware accelerators or public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results demonstrate entry-level computational throughput characteristic of first-generation AMD EPYC hardware. The instance scored 725.0 in single-core and 1744.0 in multi-core Geekbench assessments, placing it in the lower 10 percent of evaluated systems. CPU-heavy synthetic loads via stress-ng yielded 590.59 in single-threaded tests and 1179.96 under multi-core execution. PassMark evaluation recorded an overall CPU score of 3670.17 and a memory score of 1689.5. Cryptographic performance remains comparatively stable, with PassMark encryption registering 3248.98 due to hardware AES support, matching the middle 50 percent bracket.

Data handling and transactional throughput show clear limits under high-concurrency loads. Redis SET benchmarks measured 2.51 million operations per second, while PassMark database operations scored 991.42. In throughput tests, static web serving reached 2.98 GB/sec. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth reached 30.01 GB/sec alongside a write bandwidth of 14.45 GB/sec.

The m5a.xlarge offers an economical allocation of memory and vCPU resources for non-critical enterprise tasks. Because compute and memory scores reflect older architectural tiers, it exhibits lower throughput compared to modern x86 offerings. The server is well aligned for low-traffic web serving, internal utility services, dev-test environments, lightweight background workers, and caching microservices.
description: Amazon Web Services m5a.xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 7571 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz, it provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores along with 16.0 GB of DDR4 memory. It offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, a 1 Gbps baseline network speed, and zero integrated local storage. In benchmark evaluations, the m5a.xlarge exhibits modest single-core and multi-threaded throughput, registering 725.0 in single-core Geekbench and 2.51 million operations per second in Redis SET operations, though AES acceleration helps maintain average encryption performance. Due to its older generation CPU architecture, the instance represents an economical baseline capacity rather than a high-throughput processing engine. It is suitable for small-scale web servers, development staging environments, background task processing, and lightweight utility microservices.
